fact: The New Times reports the World Bank-funded Digital Acceleration Project will expand the Digital Ambassadors Programme to all 2,148 cells to train citizens to use digital devices and services, per RISA's briefing to lawmakers.

The Ministry of Education with the Ministry of ICT and Huawei launched the DigiTruck, a mobile classroom to give free digital skills training to more than 5,000 youth, women and farmers in all 30 districts over three years, part of a goal to train one million citizens.

RISA says the Digital Ambassadors Programme, run since 2017 with over 2,000 ambassadors and 60 supervisors in every district and backed by KOICA and the World Bank, has trained more than 4.5 million Rwandans in digital skills.

The deck says the Digital Ambassadors Programme, launched in 2017, has 2,000+ ambassadors across all 30 districts and has trained 2.4 million Rwandans in digital literacy (51% women), with a target of 3.8 million trainees by project close.
